First release of Folder Size Redux, a fork of Brian Oraas' (Brio) Folder Size for Windows 2.6, adapted for Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit). It shows the size of every item in File Explorer, folders included, in a companion window.

This version has only been tested on Windows 11 so far.

## Downloads

- **`FolderSizeRedux-0.1.0-x64.msi`**: the installer. It replaces Folder Size for Windows 2.6 if it is installed, and installs the Folder Size service.
- **`FolderSizeRedux-0.1.0-x64-portable.zip`**: the portable version. Extract it to a folder and run `FolderSize.exe`; nothing is installed.

The files aren't signed with a code signing certificate, so Windows may show "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

## What's new compared to Folder Size 2.6

- Dark mode, per-monitor display scaling, and support for File Explorer tabs.
- Sizes of ZIP files and other archives, used space of drives on **This PC**, and links (**Symlink**, **Junction**, **Mount point**) shown with their type.
- Sort by name (folders first, or mixed) or by size, with a default sort order in the settings.
- A **Maximum width** setting, with long names cut and shown in full in a tooltip.
- 13 languages, chosen with the **Language** setting.
- Much lighter folder reading: about 0.1 s of processing for a folder of 586 items, down from 1.2 s.
- The service asks for administrator approval (UAC) instead of failing with "Access is denied".

See the [README](https://github.com/laurentlasalle/Folder-Size-Redux#readme) for the details.
